what: powder-doser PR #190's powder-test animations, packaged for byu-vcl's vertical-lab long-form (PR #318) as 'ext' parts
format: H.264 MP4, 1280 x 720, 30 fps, no audio (the long-form's own format, so its join repeats no frames)

chapter.title: The powder tests by the standards: powder-doser's renders

clips.name: hall_flow
clips.title: Hall flowmeter and Carney funnel: flow rate
clips.label: Hall and Carney flow

byu_vcl.caption: Hall and Carney flow (ASTM B213, B964), by hand: seconds for 50 g to run out. The twin's psd.flow() predicts both; the lab doesn't measure them

steps.text: Assemble: levelled stand, Hall funnel in its holder, receiver underneath
Block the orifice with a dry finger and pour in 50.0 g of powder
Remove the finger and start the timer
Powder runs out through the 2.54 mm orifice
Stop when the last powder leaves the orifice: report s/50 g
A cohesive powder (e.g. AlSi10Mg) arches over the orifice: no flow
Swap in the Carney funnel (5.08 mm orifice, ASTM B964); refill
Release and time 50 g through the larger orifice
Report both: 'no flow' in Hall is a result, not a missing value

vertical_lab.plan: Not planned. The plan's flow numbers come from the doser: V_g and I_stop, as in [`docs/flowability/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/powder-doser/blob/0030e0d/docs/flowability/README.md) on this repo's branch at `0030e0d`.
vertical_lab.twin: [`psd.flow()`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/instruments/psd.py#L408-L443) gives Hall and Carney times for 50 g, with no Hall flow below *ff*<sub>c</sub> 3.5 and no Carney flow below 2.2 (assumed there); round 6 calls it only from a test. The proposals' lab books powder QC at a station named "Powder size and flow (sieve analysis, Hall funnel)" ([`facility.py` L76](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/facility.py#L76)); the vertical lab's `psd` station is the Mastersizer and XRF instead ([L133](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/facility.py#L133)).

clips.name: density
clips.title: Apparent and tap density to the Hausner ratio
clips.label: Apparent and tap density, Hausner ratio

byu_vcl.caption: Apparent and tap density (ASTM B212, B527) give the Hausner ratio, which the lab's runs plan takes in a graduated cylinder within a week of a run

steps.text: Assemble: levelled stand, Hall funnel 25 mm above a 25 cm³ cup
Block the orifice and load the funnel with powder
Release: powder fills the cup and overflows into the tray
Swing the funnel aside without jarring the cup
Strike off the heap: one pass of a spatula, blade upright
Weigh the powder: apparent density = mass ÷ 25 cm³
Tap density: weighed sample into a 25 mL graduated cylinder
A cam lifts the cylinder and drops it on the anvil, over and over
Hausner = TD/AD = 1.14 (above ~1.25 suggests a cohesive powder)

vertical_lab.plan: "Doser flowability, Hausner ratio", within a week of each run, 0.5–1 h ([DAL #256](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/digital-alloy-lab/issues/256)); the Hausner ratio from a graduated cylinder ([runs plan](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/cad4e6d/atomizer-runs/plan-adv-mater/measurements.md#L97-L103)).
vertical_lab.twin: `psd.flow()` returns an apparent density ([L425](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/instruments/psd.py#L425)); no tapped density.

byu_vcl.caption: Angle of repose (ISO 4324, USP <1174>), by hand: a cone on a fixed base, free-flowing then cohesive. Neither the lab nor the twin has it yet

steps.text: Assemble: fixed-diameter base, funnel clamped at a fixed height
Pour powder through the funnel; a cone builds on the base
Once the cone covers the base, the excess rolls off the edge
Measure the cone height h: angle of repose = arctan(h / r)
Clear the base; repeat with a cohesive powder (e.g. AlSi10Mg)
A cohesive powder builds a steeper, rougher cone
Steeper cone, larger angle: 47° ('poor') vs 32° ('good')
Rank on the USP <1174> flow scale: lower angle, freer flow

vertical_lab.model: Not shown (heaps in the lab model sit at an assumed angle).

byu_vcl.caption: Sieve analysis (ASTM B214): five 8 in. sieves, 150 to 45 µm, 15 min on a tapping shaker. Chapter 3's cell splits the powder; this sizes it

steps.text: Nest 200 mm test sieves, coarsest on top, pan at the bottom
Pour about 100 g (90–110 g) onto the top sieve
Fit the lid, clamp the stack and lower the tapping hammer
Shake 15 min: gyratory motion plus a tap on the lid
Stop, unclamp and unstack the sieves
Weigh the powder retained on each sieve and in the pan
Report mass % per size band and cumulative % passing
Below about 45 µm dry sieving fails: use laser diffraction

vertical_lab.model: Chapter 3 ("sieve and print"): the sieving cell, a Retsch AS 200 in a downdraft enclosure that splits the powder into jars ([`sieve_station.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/0425020/vertical-lab/sieve_station.py)).
vertical_lab.plan: No. 60, 230 and 325 and the pan, by hand, 10–20 g at a time ([runs plan](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/cad4e6d/atomizer-runs/plan-adv-mater/measurements.md#L55-L65)), within 48 h of a run ([DAL #256](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/digital-alloy-lab/issues/256)).
vertical_lab.twin: The proposals' lab has a Retsch AS 200 and a `psd` station for "sieve analysis, Hall funnel" ([`facility.py` L75-L76](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/facility.py#L75-L76)); the vertical lab has the sieve cell with its wash ([L132](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/facility.py#L132)).

byu_vcl.caption: Laser diffraction (ASTM B822, ISO 13320), drawn with a wet cell; tray E's Mastersizer disperses dry. The twin's psd.py models the same optics

steps.text: Assemble: laser, beam expander, flow cell, Fourier lens, detectors
Fill the dispersion unit with water + surfactant; pump and stir
Laser on: record the background with clean liquid
Add powder until obscuration is in range (about 5–15 %)
Particles scatter light: large ones at small angles, small at wide
A Mie (or Fraunhofer) model inverts the pattern into sizes
Report volume-weighted D10, D50, D90; compare like with like

vertical_lab.model: Chapter 4 ("the powder, checked"): the Malvern Mastersizer 3000 with the Aero S dry disperser on tray E ([`alloy_powder.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/0425020/vertical-lab/alloy_powder.py)).
vertical_lab.plan: A cross-check on one half "if a laser-diffraction instrument can be used without an ME Order" ([runs plan](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/cad4e6d/atomizer-runs/plan-adv-mater/measurements.md#L66-L67)). Utah's PSSC lab charges $5.10–$9.10 a sample, dry (this PR's costs).
vertical_lab.twin: [`psd.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/instruments/psd.py) simulates the Mastersizer: optics, dispersion, sampling and the inversion.

byu_vcl.caption: Moisture by loss on drying (USP <731>): weigh, dry at 105 °C, cool, reweigh to constant mass. Neither the lab nor the twin has it yet

steps.text: Lay out: analytical balance, oven at 105 °C, desiccator, T/RH logger
Weigh the dried, empty weighing bottle with its lid
Add about 10 g from the jar being dosed, spread thin, weigh
Into the oven with the lid off
Dry at 105 °C: water and other volatiles leave the powder
Lid on, cool to room temperature in the desiccator
Reweigh
Dry 1 h more, cool, reweigh: repeat until two weighings agree
LOD = mass lost ÷ moist sample mass; record T/RH with it

vertical_lab.plan: Not planned (the plan records how many days each sample was stored, for oxygen pick-up).

clips.name: ft4_shear
clips.title: FT4 shear cell: yield locus and flow function
clips.label: FT4 shear cell

byu_vcl.caption: FT4 shear cell (ASTM D7891): the yield locus and the flow function ffc. The twin estimates ffc from a Bond number; this is how it's measured

steps.text: Assemble: base with load-cell seat, drive tower, split glass vessel
Fill the 25 mm split vessel with powder
Condition: blade spirals down and up for a uniform, loose packing
Vented piston consolidates the bed to 9 kPa; air escapes
Split the vessel: excess powder leaves a level 10 mL bed
Bladed shear head moves down; its blades enter the bed
Pre-shear at 9 kPa; shear to failure at e.g. 7, 6, 5, 4, 3 kPa
Yield locus + Mohr circles give σc and σ1; ffc = σ1 / σc

vertical_lab.plan: Not planned; a send-out ($650 a sample at Micromeritics, this PR's costs).
vertical_lab.twin: `psd.flow()` sets *ff*<sub>c</sub> = 3.7 Bo<sup>−0.27</sup> from a Bond number (Capece et al., "as recalled; check" there; [L424](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/blob/938115f/vertical-lab/twin/instruments/psd.py#L424)), and gates Hall and Carney flow on it.

clips.name: ring_shear
clips.title: Schulze ring shear tester: yield locus and flow function
clips.label: Ring shear tester

byu_vcl.caption: Schulze ring shear tester (ASTM D6773): the same ffc, for a cohesive powder. Sent out at about $650 a sample; no station in the lab

steps.text: Assemble: drive base, turntable, annular shear cell with floor bars
Fill the ring, then scrape the powder level with the rim
Lay the annular lid, bars down, on the powder
Tie rods hold the lid; weights add the normal load
Ring turns, lid is held: pre-shear at 6 kPa, shear at 4.5, 3, 1.5 kPa
Yield locus + Mohr circles give σc and σ1; ffc = σ1 / σc

vertical_lab.plan: Not planned; a send-out, as for the FT4.
